title: SPEC A implementation: config staging/live promotion

completion_criteria.text: SPEC A section 7's five cutover preconditions are all closed and verified, with the *session* gitignore pattern narrowed BEFORE the hook file it hides is adopted.
The promote verb is implemented with pre-swap validation, rollback by rename, and the LIVE receipt, and the bootstrap resolves outside releases/.
SessionStart and Stop converge hooks are registered, and a drift report reaches session context when live differs from main.
The settings.json ownership manifest and the separate capture verb are implemented, with unknown keys defaulting to LIVE WINS and flagged rather than dropped.
The cutover runs serially in a session doing nothing else: the first release is built and validated with zero live change, then every entry link is swapped in one pass.
All 10 of SPEC A's acceptance criteria pass, with criterion 10 verified by diffing the live tree against the release rather than asserted.
Every unit ships through a PR opened by pr.mjs pr-create, stacked with --base <parent-branch> where one change blocks another.

spine.active_goal: Fully implement and ship SPEC A (config staging/live promotion) via a dedicated small dynamic workflow, using stacked PRs where changes block each other.

open_risks.text: Run the cutover serially in a session doing nothing else — it hot-swaps live-linked hooks, lib and workflows, so parallel subagents editing those paths can break every running session including the one doing the work.

Narrow the unanchored *session* pattern BEFORE adopting hooks/session-config-drift-check.sh — adoption done first appears to succeed and the file still never enters a release, because git archive carries only tracked content.

Open every stacked child manually with pr.mjs pr-create --base <parent-branch> — the engine has no stacking: merge-policy returns HUMAN_GATED unconditionally, every PR opens on baseBranch, and pr.mjs has no retarget verb.

Retarget each stacked child explicitly once its parent merges — deleteBranchOnMerge is false on this repo so GitHub's auto-retarget never fires; gh pr edit --base passes the bash gate today, which is the accidental route SPEC B section 5.5 closes.

Name the rule divergence at merge time rather than resolving it silently — 0265 merges dependent chains with merge-commit while branching.md still states squash-on-merge as the unqualified default, and that amendment ships with SPEC B Part IV.

Expect suite totals to shift when the gitignore narrows — npm test globs the filesystem, so the previously hidden session-config-drift-check test starts counting; reconcile per file, never by raw total.

key_decisions.title: The workflow fan-out boundary is any write to a live-linked path, not the cutover alone

out_of_scope: Building SPEC B Part IV's stacked-PR machinery to serve this work - stacking here is manual via the convention, and 0271 orders SPEC A to land before any SPEC B unit
Editing mitosis.js or the parallel engine, which SPEC B governs
